lesson.label: 🧠 Brainstorming questions (Câu hỏi nên nghĩ trước buổi học)
items: Where’s your hometown, and **how often do you go back?**
What do you **miss most about your hometown** when you’re away?
Would you rather **live in a big city, by the sea or in the mountains**? Why?
How **has your hometown changed** since you were a child?

lesson.label: 📖 Bài học chính
lesson.title: 1. City life or beach life?
lesson.context: ***Context:*** *Minh, from Hà Nội, and Vy, from Quy Nhơn, are stuck in a taxi in rush-hour traffic.*
lines: We’ve only moved ten metres in fifteen minutes. **I can’t stand** this traffic!
Honestly, Hà Nội is a real **concrete jungle**. In Quy Nhơn, I’d be home by now, probably relaxing on the beach with a coconut.
**Stop rubbing it in!** But come on, you like it here a little bit.
OK, **I’ll admit it**. The food is amazing, and **there’s always something going on**.
Exactly. And there are **way more job opportunities**. Half my friends from university moved here for work.
True, but city life can be **exhausting**. Two hours **stuck in traffic** every day, and all that **air pollution**…
**Fair point.** So what’s a normal day like back home?

**Super chilled.** My parents’ house is **a stone’s throw from** the beach, so I **wake up to the sound of** the waves. Every morning, my mum goes to the fish market and **haggles** for the freshest fish.
Stop, you’re making me hungry! But don’t you get bored? I’d miss going out late at night.
Haha, **that’s the only downside**. Most places close by nine. But people there are **really close**. If you’re sick, the whole street **turns up** with soup.
That’s so sweet. In my building, people don’t even **make eye contact** in the lift.
Has Hà Nội changed much since you were a kid?
**Yeah, a lot.** Some areas are **almost unrecognisable**. The rice fields near my grandma’s house are now huge **apartment blocks**.
Same in Quy Nhơn. Tourists keep **flooding in**, and new resorts are **popping up** all along the coast.
Well, **I’d swap** this traffic **for** a beach **any day**!

lesson.label: Tell us about your hometown
head: Purposes
Phrases
rows: **Where is it? What’s it known for?**

• ***I’m from…, a busy city / a coastal city / a small town in…***
• ***It’s about … hours from… by bus / plane.***
• ***It’s best known for… / It’s famous for…***
• ***It’s not very well-known, but…***

• ***Life there is much slower / busier than in…***
• ***There’s always something going on.***
• ***After work, most people…***
**What do you love? What wears you down?**

• ***What I love most about it is…***
• ***The best thing about living there is…***
• ***The one thing I can’t stand is…***
• ***The only downside is that…***
**What are the people like? How do you feel about it?**

• ***People there are really friendly / close / hard-working.***
• ***Everyone looks out for each other.***
• ***Whenever I go back, I feel at home.***

lesson.title: 2. Then and now
lesson.context: ***Context:*** *Quân, from Sài Gòn, and Ngọc, from Đà Lạt, are friends. They’re having coffee after the long weekend.*
lines: You’re back! How was home? Was it cold up there?
Really nice, thanks. I ate **way too much**, **as usual**. But it **wasn’t as cold as I expected**. It’s **much warmer than** when I was a kid. I wore a T-shirt most of the day.
In Đà Lạt? I didn’t expect that.
Yeah. My mum thinks it’s because they’ve built so much. A lot of the hills near our house **are covered in** greenhouses now.
That’s a bit sad. I always **think of** Đà Lạt **as** pine trees and fog.
Some parts are still like that. But at weekends, it gets **really crowded**. Lots of people **drive up** from Sài Gòn, and it’s **really hard to find a parking space**.
**To be honest**, I was one of them last month.
Haha, that’s OK. **It’s good for business.** A few of my **old classmates** have **moved back** and **opened** their own coffee shops. Ten years ago, everyone wanted to leave.
That’s nice. Sài Gòn has changed a lot too. It **feels like a different city** every few years.
The metro, **for sure**. I used to spend an hour on my motorbike every morning, **stuck in traffic**. Now it **only takes** about twenty minutes, and I can listen to music on the way.
That’s **a big improvement**. Is there anything you don’t like?
They **turned** the market near my parents’ house **into** a shopping mall. It’s **handy**, I guess, but **it’s not the same**. I used to go there with my grandma every Sunday.
**I understand.** It’s usually the small places you miss.

homework.title: Part 1: Vocab check
homework.instructions: Fill in each blank with a phrase from the word bank. Use each phrase once.
homework.context: Thảo has just moved from Huế to Sài Gòn for a new job. Her friend Nam calls to ask how she's doing.
lines: Hi Thảo! How's life in Sài Gòn?
Good, but busy! There's always {something going on}. Last night I went to a night market, and this weekend there's a music festival near my flat.
That sounds fun. Do you like your new job?
Yes, I do. There are {way more} jobs for designers here than in Huế. That's why I moved.
Really nice. It's {a stone's throw from} a big park, so I go for a walk there every morning.
That's great. Is there anything you don't like?
The traffic. Yesterday I was {stuck in traffic} for an hour on my way home. I really {can't stand} it.
Well, Huế is quiet and slow, {as usual}. I walked by the river after work today. It was so peaceful.
{Stop rubbing it in}! I really miss those walks.
Huế is changing too, though. Some streets near our old school are {almost unrecognisable} now. New hotels and cafés are {popping up} everywhere.
Really? I've only been away for two months!
Haha, it's not that fast. But it's much busier than before. So how do you feel after two months there?
Much better. The first few weeks were really {exhausting}. Everything was new, and I was tired all the time. But now I'm starting to feel at home.

homework.title: Part 2: Listening
homework.intro: Listen to Lily talking about her hometown, then do Parts A and B.

script.text: Hi, I'm Lily. I grew up in Mudgee, a small ==farming== town about four hours from Sydney, in Australia. When I was a kid, I loved it. We had a big garden, and my brother and I rode our bikes everywhere. But when I was a teenager, ==I found it a bit boring==. There was only one cinema, and the last bus left at six o'clock.

So when I was nineteen, I moved to Sydney for ==university==. Now I work at a bank in the city centre. I love the restaurants and the beaches here, but ==the rent is really expensive==. I share a small flat with two friends, and my bedroom is smaller than my parents' bathroom!

I go back home three or four times a year. Last Christmas, I was really surprised. My town has ==changed== a lot. ==There are lots of new wine bars and restaurants==, and tourists come from Sydney every weekend. My dad's old shop is now a ==café==. He wasn't happy about it at first, but ==now he goes there every morning== for his coffee.
Some things haven't changed, though. ==People still say hello to everyone== in the street, and my mum still knows all the neighbours' names. In my building in Sydney, I don't know anyone.
Would I move back? ==Maybe one day, when I have children.== For now, I'm happy in the city.

questions.q: How did Lily feel about her town when she was a teenager?
options: She loved riding her bike everywhere.
She thought there wasn't much to do.
She wanted to work on a farm.
questions.why: “When I was a teenager, I found it a bit boring.”

questions.q: What does Lily say about her life in Sydney?
options: She lives alone in a small flat.
Her bedroom is bigger than her parents' bathroom.
It costs a lot of money to live there.
There were lots of new places to eat and drink.
Her dad had opened a new café.
There weren't many tourists in town.
questions.why: “There are lots of new wine bars and restaurants.”

questions.q: How does Lily's dad feel about the café now?
options: He is still unhappy about it.
He likes it and goes there often.
questions.why: “Now he goes there every morning for his coffee.”

questions.q: What hasn't changed in Lily's hometown?
options: People are still friendly to each other.
The last bus still leaves at six o'clock.
Her mum still lives in the same building.
questions.why: “People still say hello to everyone in the street.”

questions.q: Will Lily move back to her hometown?
options: Yes, she's moving back next year.
No, she wants to stay in Sydney forever.
Maybe, at some point in the future.
questions.why: “Maybe one day, when I have children.”
